title: How the barcode changed retail
text: Few inventions have transformed shopping {{1}} thoroughly as the barcode. Before its introduction in the 1970s, shop assistants typed every price {{2}} hand, and queues were endless. The barcode allowed retailers to track stock automatically, {{3}} meant fewer empty shelves and lower prices. Consumers initially feared the technology {{4}} be used to spy on their purchases, but such concerns soon faded. Today the humble stripe pattern appears {{5}} everywhere, from hospital wristbands to luggage tags. Researchers estimate that barcodes save the retail industry billions each year, {{6}} is a remarkable return on a simple idea. It is hard to imagine modern shopping {{7}} it. Like many great inventions, the barcode succeeded not because it was clever, {{8}} because it solved a real problem reliably.
